body.statement: For every \(S\in\mathcal I\) and every mechanism in \(\mathfrak M_{\mathcal I}(G)\), \(\det(C_{S,S})\ne0\) and \(K_S^{B,\varepsilon}(x)=\mathcal L(R_S(C)\varepsilon+T_S(C)x)\). Moreover, \(R_S(C)\varepsilon=X_{X\setminus S}-T_S(C)X_S\) observationally. Hence the observational law together with \(\{T_S(C):S\in\mathcal I\}\) determines the entire joint tuple of affine response kernels, including every cancellation and every observationally invisible source.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(S\in\mathcal I\), put \(U=V\setminus S\) and \(O=X\setminus S\), and set \(A=Q^{-1}\).  The inclusion \(\varnothing\in\mathcal I\) and Assumption \(\texttt{ass:regime-solvability}\) give \(\det Q\ne0\), while the same assumption at \(S\) gives \(\det Q_{U,U}\ne0\).  Empty matrices have determinant one throughout.  Block elimination in the order \((S,U)\) gives
\[
 \det Q=\det(Q_{U,U})
 \det\!\left(Q_{S,S}-Q_{S,U}Q_{U,U}^{-1}Q_{U,S}\right)
\]
and the block-inverse identity gives
\[
 A_{S,S}=\left(Q_{S,S}-Q_{S,U}Q_{U,U}^{-1}Q_{U,S}\right)^{-1}.
\]
Because \(S\subseteq X\), \(C_{S,S}=A_{S,S}\).  Therefore
\[
 \det(C_{S,S})=\frac{\det(Q_{U,U})}{\det Q}\ne0.                    \tag{1}
\]

The \((U,S)\) block of \(QA=I_N\) is
\[
 Q_{U,U}A_{U,S}+Q_{U,S}A_{S,S}=0.
\]
Since \(Q_{U,S}=-B_{U,S}\), equation (1) yields
\[
 T_S(C)=C_{O,S}C_{S,S}^{-1}
       =\bigl[Q_{U,U}^{-1}B_{U,S}\bigr]_{O,:}.                       \tag{2}
\]
The \((U,U)\) block of \(QA=I_N\) similarly gives
\[
 A_{U,U}-Q_{U,U}^{-1}B_{U,S}A_{S,U}=Q_{U,U}^{-1}.                    \tag{3}
\]
By Definition \(\texttt{def:intervention-response-maps}\), equations (2)--(3) say that \(R_S(C)\) has zero columns on \(S\) and
\[
 R_S(C)_{:,U}=(Q_{U,U}^{-1})_{O,U}.                                  \tag{4}
\]

Assumption \(\texttt{ass:perfect-intervention}\) replaces precisely the equations in \(S\).  Hence the remaining structural equations are
\[
 Q_{U,U}V_U=\varepsilon_U+B_{U,S}x.
\]
Equations (2) and (4) imply, on the structural probability space,
\[
 X_O^{\operatorname{do}(X_S=x)}=R_S(C)\varepsilon+T_S(C)x.
\]
Taking laws proves
\[
 K_S^{B,\varepsilon}(x)
 =\mathcal L\bigl(R_S(C)\varepsilon+T_S(C)x\bigr).                   \tag{5}
\]
In the observational regime \(X=C\varepsilon\), so the definition of \(R_S\) gives the samplewise identity
\[
 R_S(C)\varepsilon=X_O-T_S(C)X_S.                                   \tag{6}
\]
Thus the observational law determines the law on the right of (6), and (5) determines every response kernel once the finite collection of matrices \(T_S(C)\) is supplied.  Finally, if \(C_{:,i}=0\), then both \(C_{O,i}\) and \(C_{S,i}\) vanish, whence \(R_S(C)_{:,i}=0\) for every \(S\).  Thus an observationally invisible source stays invisible under every allowed intervention.  No expectation, moment, centering, positivity, boundary, or limiting argument is used.  The identities also cover \(S=\varnothing\), \(O=\varnothing\), and zero residual columns under the stated empty-matrix conventions.
body.justification: The algebraic resolvent identity reduces every intervention kernel to an observational residual law and a finite response matrix without using means, centering, or moments.
body.gap: Published solvability semantics do not themselves give the principal-resolvent pushforward, source-visibility consequence, or the simultaneous representation used by the compiler.
body.consumer: Both exact and downward-closed compilers compare one observational mixture and finitely many response matrices rather than aligning latent sources separately in every regime.
